subject: Cloud Computing
title: The Principle of Least Privilege
description: A 60-second lesson on The Principle of Least Privilege.

hook.text: A junior developer has admin access to the production database. What could go wrong? Everything.

buildup.text: Least privilege means giving users and services only the minimum permissions they need to do their job.

discovery.text: If an account is compromised, least privilege limits the blast radius. The attacker can only reach a small area.

twist.text: In practice, most teams give too many permissions because restricting access slows down development.

climax.text: The balance between security and productivity is the eternal struggle. Least privilege leans toward safety.

punchline.text: Give the minimum access needed. No more, no less.

quiz.question: Why is the principle of least privilege often violated in practice?
options: Restricting access slows development, so teams grant broad permissions
Cloud providers don't support fine-grained permission controls
Least privilege only applies to physical access, not digital systems

details.summary: Least privilege means granting users and services only the minimum permissions they need to perform their tasks. Over-permissioned accounts create massive attack surfaces that adversaries exploit to move laterally through cloud environments.
details.whyItMatters: Excess permissions turn a single compromised credential into a full-environment breach. Least privilege limits blast radius and is a core tenet of zero trust.
takeaways: Grant only the minimum permissions needed for each task
Excess permissions expand the blast radius of breaches
Regular audits help identify and remove unused access

faq.question: How do you implement least privilege at scale?
faq.answer: Use role-based access control with narrowly scoped roles, automate permission reviews, leverage cloud-native tools that flag unused permissions, and adopt just-in-time access where elevated privileges expire automatically after a time window.

faq.question: Why is least privilege hard to maintain?
faq.answer: Permissions accumulate over time as employees change roles or projects add temporary access. Without automated auditing, organizations suffer privilege creep where accounts accumulate far more access than they currently need.
